records.public_safe_text: officer medina #1478 and officer herrera #1571 were dispatched to 7101 gateway west on a pedestrian collision. officers were then informed of the correct address of 10727 gateway west where the witness followed the vehicle involved. officers were given a description of the vehicle involved(unit 1). officers located unit 1 driver fueling up at the gas station(murphy's usa). officers stopped and met with the unit 1 driver and later with the witness. unit 1 driver denied hitting anyone or anything, however did admit to having an incident on the interstate where a vehicle cut him off and he was going to physically fight the other driver, however stated that the other subject reached over to his waist as if retreiving some kind of weapon, therefore the unit 1 driver fled driving. unit 1 driver did not have an explanation to his missing passenger mirror. unit 1 driver did not have an explanation as to the black marking on the right side(passenger sliding door) of unit 1, however later advised that the damage was there already. the witness approached the officers who advised that as the witness drove along the interstate 10, the witness observed the unit 1 and another vehicle pulled over to the right shoulder. the witness then observed the unit 1 leave the scene and hitting the pedestrian(driver to the other vehicle). the witness said she observed the door to the pedestrian's vehicle open as the unit 1 fled westbound to the murphy's usa gas station. officers could not locate a victim or other complainant to this incident. the officers could not locate the mirror to the unit 1 on the interstate. witness: beatriz sandoval espinoza, [date], 719 uranio, el paso texas 79928, ph#[phone]

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] at about 1102 hours, i, investigating officer, corporal stephen bean - #318, university of north texas police department, responded to the area of [roadway], located in the city and county of denton, tx. upon arrival i observed (vehicle #1) a silver in color ford f-150 bearing texas lp #1kttz that was stopped at an angle facing southeast in the #2 lane (right) with the front passenger tire in contact with the south curb to the point that the tire displayed a noticeable bulge from the pressure. i observed a b/f later identified as the pedestrian (tori faith brackens, b/f, dob: [date]) laying on the ground against the south curb behind the silver f-150. brackens appeared to be injured and stated that her side was hurting referencing her left hip and leg. the driver of vehicle #1 was sitting in the passenger seat, and was unable to immediately exit the vehicle due to the fact that he is wheelchair bound. he was identified as kyle aaron lightsey, w/m, dob: [date], and observed to be the sole occupant of the vehicle. lightsey stated that he was the driver of the ford, which was confirmed by the four other witnesses who provided written statements, as well as brackens. all parties including the four witnesses stated that [roadway] from the south traveling north, and that lightsey was operating the ford f-150 and traveling eastbound in the #1 lane (left) prior to the crash. according to brackens' (pedestrian) account she was walking out of the university of north texas, business leadership building located on the south side of this location and that she observed the driver of vehicle #1 stopped on the west side of the cross walk so that people could cross, she began looking down at [roadway] on the east side of the crosswalk traveling north. brackens further states that upon reaching the center line that divides the #1 and #2 main travel lanes she was struck by the truck near the front right quarter panel area and it impacted her hip and thigh on her left side. lightsey stated during a subsequent interview that after he stopped to allow pedestrians to cross at the cross walk he proceeded eastbound, and that he was focused on persons approaching the cross walk on the north side of the roadway to make sure no one ran into the cross walk. lightsey stated that he heard a thump on the right (south) side of his truck and realized he hit brackens and noticed his passenger side mirror was folded in. lightsey estimated brackens to be 10-15 feet passed the cross walk on the east side, of which was the given estimate by a witness on scene and also confirmed by brackens. lightsey estimated his speed prior to the crash to be approximately 15 mph. a witness in her statement details that she observed the truck to be speeding. the proximity of the truck at rest on the west side of the cross walk to the estimated point of impact would be an estimated 25-30 feet in total length of travel prior to the crash from a stopped position. brackens was unable to provide any details about the movement of the truck, due to her focus being on her cell [roadway]. there were no signs of evasive action or an actual point of impact. no damage was observed on the truck, there was a small scratch near the front passenger side tire well that was photographed, though lightsey states it was preexisting damage. i did not detect any scuff or roadway markings that i believe produced during this crash. during my interview with both parties, i did not detect and neither admitted to the use of drugs or alcohol. crosswalk traveling north. brackens further states that upon reaching the center line that divides the #1 and #2 main travel lanes she was struck by the truck near the front right quarter panel area and it impacted her hip and thigh on her left side. lightsey stated during a subsequent interview that after he stopped to allow pedestrians to cross at the cross walk he proceeded eastbound, and that he was focused on persons approaching the cross walk on the north side of the roadway to make sure no one ran into the cross walk. lightsey stated that he heard a thump on the right (south) side of his truck and realized he hit brackens and noticed his passenger side mirror was folded in. lightsey estimated brackens to be 10-15 feet passed the cross walk on the east side, of which was the given records.public_safe_text: police responded to [roadway] for a call for a major accident. i arrived on scene to observe my listed pedestrian victim (to be refered to as v1 for this report.) sitting on the ground surrounded by several people. v1 appeared to have minor injuries but was bleeding in several places. i called for ems to arrive on scene to check on v1. witnesses to the crash (information for them is listed on the keycard.) all stated that they observed unit 1 run over v1 in the parking lot. one of the witnesses (w2 on the key card.) stated that v1 was actually laying in the roadway prior to being struck by unit 1, when asked why v1 was doing this w2 stated that she thought v1 was ""trying to be cute or funny."". unit 1 was observed driving through the parking lot at a high rate of speed according to the witnesses and w2 stated that she believed unit 1 was deliberately the staff at the bar that was the incident location stated that v1 and his group (which included w1.) had all been drinking so this may have contributed to v1's behavoir. as far as why v1 and his party were outside the bar at the time of the crash, they were there so an uber could come to pick them up to take them home. the entire time i was on scene v1 was not responsive to my cover officer's questions and due to him being hit by unit 1, [medical facility]. officers on scene assisting me kept tabs on the witnesses and gathered v1's information for me. sgt. b. branham #3391 was notified of the situation. tid was contacted and det. j. reyna #2177 made scene. csi was requested and m. loveridge #9425 made the scene to process. at this time the only information that is available regarding unit 1 is what is listed. witnesses stated that unit 1 [roadway].

records.deidentified_narrative: [roadway] roadway which contains two eastbound and two westbound lanes divided by a concrete raised median. unit 1 was traveling eastbound on the #2 lane at the 7300 block of viscount. unit #2 (pedestrian) was crossing the roadway (southbound) on foot at the 7300 block of viscount. as unit #2 crossed both the westbound and eastbound lanes, it was reported by unit #1's driver, that unit #2 fell backward upon tripping on the curb. as unit #2 fell backward, unit #1 was passing. unit #1 then struck unit #2 as a result, of unit #2 reportedly falling backward. unit #2 was struck with the front right side of the vehicle. the investigating officers observed damage to the hood and windshield. the officers also noted that one of the shoes was located approximately 50 feet east from the point of impact, the other shoe was located in the bushes by the sidewalk. an article of clothing believed to be unit #2's head cover, was observed attached to the windshield wiper. unit #2 was transported to umc via fms form the scene. a follow up investigation revealed unit #2 sustained internal injury to her skull as well as bleeding to her brain. officers spoke with all three occupants of unit #1, and believed that their version of event was consistent with the evidence recovered at the scene. officers did not locate any evidence at the scene contradicting with their statements. the driver of unit #1 was cited and requested another driver to operate the vehicle. special traffic investigation would conduct a follow up to the pedestrian's injuries.
